Integrability supplies a strictly descending secant of log k; concavity bounds the right tail by its affine continuation, so the moments are finite. Tonelli gives ∫∫S(s+t)dsdt=∫uS(u)du=E[X²]/2. Equality makes the continuous nonnegative deficit vanish pointwise; −log S is then continuous and additive, so the survival law is exponential with a strictly positive rate. Exponentials attain equality.

On every compact interval of positive a, the derivative integrands through order two are dominated by an integrable polynomial times an exponential. Differentiating ψ=a/M₀ cancels the two terms linear in M₁, giving (2M₁²−M₀M₂)/(a³M₀³). The normalized tilt is a positive log-concave probability density, so the numerator is nonnegative.

The substitution t=as and boundedness of h give M₀(a)/a→h(0)=1 by dominated convergence. If ψ″=0 at any a, equality for the tilted law makes h exponential on the entire half-line by continuity, and integrability forces a positive decay rate α. Then ψ′=α>0. Otherwise ψ″>0 everywhere; the endpoint limit and a strict secant comparison give ψ′(a)>(ψ(a)−1)/a, including when ψ(a)=1.
